entries.title: Geography: latitude and longitude
entries.text: Latitude describes angular position north or south of the equator, from −90° to 90°. Longitude describes angular position east or west of the prime meridian, usually from −180° to 180°. A coordinate alone is not a live location fix; its time, source and accuracy matter.

entries.title: History: interpreting sources
entries.text: Historical claims should be checked against dated sources and their context. A primary source comes from the period or event being studied; a secondary source analyzes earlier evidence. Both can contain bias or mistakes. Distinguish documented events, disputed interpretations and unknown details.

entries.title: Everyday information: forecasts and news
entries.text: A forecast is a probabilistic prediction, not a guarantee. A publication date is not proof that a report is accurate. Separate source headlines from independently verified reporting. Offline reference material is not a live news service. Do not infer current conditions from old cached information.
